places.name: Lisbon
places.summary: Portugal's hilly capital on the Tagus estuary, with historic quarters, viewpoints, trams and a lively food scene. The natural base for Sintra, Cascais and Setúbal day trips.
facts: Driving and parking in the centre are hard; use metro, trams, trains and walking
Lisboa Card covers public transport and many museum entries
Wear grippy shoes: the polished limestone pavements are slippery when wet
Many museums and monuments close on Mondays

places.name: Alfama
places.summary: Lisbon's oldest district, a maze of steep lanes, stairways and small squares below the castle. Best explored on foot, ideally combined with the castle, the cathedral and the miradouros.
facts: Free to wander; allow 1.5–2 h
Steep cobbled streets: comfortable shoes
Lively at night with fado houses and small restaurants
Tram 28 passes through but is usually crowded

places.name: São Jorge Castle (Castelo de São Jorge)
places.summary: Moorish-era hilltop castle crowning Alfama, with restored walls, towers and the best panoramic views over the city and river.
facts: Ticket ~€15
Queues build mid-morning; go at opening or late afternoon
Walk up through Alfama or take bus 737 from Praça da Figueira
Allow 1–1.5 h

places.name: Lisbon Cathedral (Sé)
places.summary: Fortress-like Romanesque cathedral from the 12th century, the city's oldest church, on the way between Baixa and Alfama.
facts: Small fee for nave/cloister/treasury
Tram 28 stops outside
Quick stop of 20–40 min

places.name: Praça do Comércio & Baixa
places.summary: Grand riverside square rebuilt after the 1755 earthquake, opening onto the Pombaline grid of the Baixa with Rua Augusta and its triumphal arch.
facts: Free; Rua Augusta Arch viewing platform is ticketed
Nice at sunset by the river (Cais das Colunas)
Easy walk to Chiado, Alfama and the Santa Justa Lift

places.name: Santa Justa Lift
places.summary: Neo-Gothic iron elevator from 1902 linking the Baixa with Carmo square, with a small viewing deck on top.
facts: Ride included in the Carris/Metro 24h ticket
Queues are often long; you can walk up to the top deck from Largo do Carmo instead
Allow 20–40 min

places.name: Carmo Convent ruins
places.summary: Roofless Gothic church left as a ruin after the 1755 earthquake, with a small archaeological museum inside. A striking reminder of the disaster in the heart of Chiado.
facts: Ticket ~€5
Combine with Chiado and the Santa Justa Lift top deck
Allow 30–45 min

places.name: Chiado & Bairro Alto
places.summary: Elegant shopping and café quarter with historic theatres and bookshops, next to Bairro Alto's grid of narrow streets that fills with bars at night.
facts: Bertrand, said to be the oldest operating bookshop, is on Rua Garrett
Bairro Alto is quiet by day and very busy late at night
Walk up from Baixa or take the Glória funicular

places.name: Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara
places.wiki: Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara
places.summary: Garden terrace at the top of the Glória funicular with a broad view east over Baixa to the castle.
facts: Free
Great at sunset and after dark
Glória funicular from Restauradores goes right up

places.name: Miradouro de Santa Luzia
places.summary: Tiled, bougainvillea-draped terrace over Alfama's rooftops and the Tagus; Portas do Sol viewpoint is just next door.
facts: Free
Tram 28 stops here
Morning light is best for photos
Senhora do Monte and Graça viewpoints are higher up nearby

places.name: Tram 28
places.summary: Vintage yellow tram rattling from Martim Moniz through Graça, Alfama, Baixa and Estrela. Iconic, but often packed with tourists.
facts: Single fare bought on board ~€3; included in 24h transport ticket
Board at Martim Moniz early morning to get a seat
Watch for pickpockets
Tram 12 or 24 are calmer alternatives

places.name: Fado evening in Alfama
places.summary: Live performance of fado, Lisbon's melancholic UNESCO-listed song genre, in a small Alfama or Mouraria tavern over dinner.
facts: Book a table for the evening; many houses have a minimum spend
Silence is expected during songs
Shows usually start around 20:00–21:00
The Fado Museum in Alfama gives background

places.name: Jerónimos Monastery
places.summary: UNESCO-listed Manueline monastery funded by the spice trade, with an extraordinary two-storey cloister and the tomb of Vasco da Gama in the church.
facts: Ticket ~€18 for the cloister; church entry free
Book online and arrive at opening — queues are long
Pastéis de Belém bakery is a few steps away
Combine with Belém Tower and Padrão in a half-day

places.name: Belém Tower
places.summary: Early-16th-century Manueline fortress on the Tagus shore, the symbol of Portugal's Age of Discovery and a UNESCO site with Jerónimos.
facts: Ticket ~€10; book a timed slot online
Interior is small with a narrow one-way stair; the outside is the main attraction
Allow 45 min including queue

places.name: Padrão dos Descobrimentos
places.summary: Huge riverside monument to the navigators, with Henry the Navigator at the prow and a giant compass-rose map inlaid in the square.
facts: Free to see from outside; lift to the top is ticketed
Between Jerónimos and Belém Tower
Allow 20–30 min

places.name: MAAT (Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology)
places.wiki: Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology
places.summary: Wave-shaped contemporary museum on the Belém riverfront with changing exhibitions, plus the old Tejo power station building; its walkable roof is a fine viewpoint.
facts: Ticket ~€11 for both buildings
Closed Tuesdays
Rooftop walkway is free to climb

places.name: National Coach Museum
places.summary: One of the world's finest collections of royal carriages, from gilded baroque coaches to 19th-century berlins, in Belém.
facts: Ticket ~€8
Good rainy-day stop in Belém
Allow about 1 h

places.name: LX Factory
places.summary: Converted 19th-century industrial complex under the 25 de Abril Bridge, now full of shops, studios, cafés and the Ler Devagar bookstore.
facts: Free entry
Busiest on Sunday with a market
Between Baixa and Belém (tram 15 to Alcântara)

places.name: Time Out Market (Mercado da Ribeira)
places.summary: Food hall in the old Ribeira market at Cais do Sodré, with stalls from well-known Lisbon chefs and producers.
facts: Very busy at lunch and dinner; go off-peak
The traditional fresh market section runs in the mornings
Next to Cais do Sodré station (trains to Cascais)

places.name: Calouste Gulbenkian Museum
places.summary: Superb private collection from Egyptian antiquities and Islamic art to Lalique jewellery and European paintings, set in modernist gardens.
facts: Ticket ~€10–15; free on Sunday afternoons
Closed Tuesdays
The gardens are free and peaceful
Metro São Sebastião

places.name: National Tile Museum (Museu Nacional do Azulejo)
places.summary: History of Portuguese azulejo tiles in a former convent, with a lavish gilded chapel and a long tiled panorama of pre-earthquake Lisbon.
facts: Ticket ~€8
Closed Mondays
Out of the centre to the east: bus or taxi
Allow 1–1.5 h

places.name: Lisbon Oceanarium
places.summary: Large aquarium in Parque das Nações built for Expo 98, centred on a huge open-ocean tank with sharks, rays and a sunfish.
facts: Ticket ~€25; buy online
Metro Oriente; combine with a riverside walk and cable car in Parque das Nações
Good for kids and rainy days
Allow 2 h

places.name: Cristo Rei (Almada)
places.summary: Giant Christ statue across the Tagus in Almada; a lift takes you to a platform with a sweeping view of Lisbon and the 25 de Abril Bridge.
facts: Small fee for the lift to the platform
Reach by car or ferry from Cais do Sodré to Cacilhas then bus
Late afternoon light on Lisbon is best

places.name: Sintra
places.summary: UNESCO-listed romantic town in the forested Sintra hills, packed with palaces and fantasy estates. Stay overnight to see it before and after the day-trip crowds.
facts: Parking is very scarce; train from Lisbon Rossio (~40 min) or park at the edge
Bus 434 loops the centre, Moorish Castle and Pena
Try travesseiros and queijadas pastries
Book Pena tickets in advance
places.season: The hills are often misty and cooler than Lisbon; bring a layer.

places.name: Cascais
places.summary: Former fishing village turned upmarket seaside town with small beaches, a marina, a citadel and a pleasant old centre. A relaxed base with direct trains to Lisbon.
facts: Train from Cais do Sodré ~40 min
Free BiCas bikes / coastal bike path to Guincho
Paid parking garages in town

places.name: Estoril
places.summary: Belle-époque resort next to Cascais known for its casino, gardens and seafront promenade linking the two towns.
facts: Walk the 3 km Paredão seafront promenade to Cascais
Tamariz beach is right by the station
Casino open evenings

places.name: Pena Palace
places.summary: Brightly coloured 19th-century romantic palace on a peak above Sintra, with lavish royal interiors and a vast wooded park with viewpoints like Cruz Alta.
facts: Palace + park ~€20; timed entry slot for the palace — book online
Arrive for the first slot to beat crowds
Steep walk or shuttle from the park gate to the palace
Allow 2–3 h with the park
places.caution: Road up is narrow and congested; use bus 434 or a tuk-tuk rather than driving.

places.name: Quinta da Regaleira
places.summary: Mystical early-20th-century estate with a gothic mansion, grottoes, tunnels and the famous Initiation Well spiralling down into the earth.
facts: Ticket ~€15; book online, queues can be long
5–10 min walk from Sintra centre
Bring a light for the tunnels
Allow 1.5–2 h

places.name: Moorish Castle
places.summary: Ruined medieval castle walls snaking along a granite ridge, with huge views to Pena, the Atlantic and Lisbon on clear days.
facts: Ticket ~€12; combo tickets with Pena available
Lots of steps, little shade
Easy to combine with Pena (10 min walk)

places.name: Sintra National Palace
places.summary: Medieval royal palace in the town centre, recognisable by its two huge conical kitchen chimneys, with superb Mudéjar tiles and painted ceilings.
facts: Ticket ~€13
Right in the centre; good rainy-day option
Allow about 1 h

places.name: Monserrate Palace & Gardens
places.summary: Exotic Moorish-Gothic palace set in a landscaped botanical park with plants from around the world; much calmer than Pena.
facts: Ticket ~€12
4 km west of the centre; bus 435 or car with parking
Allow 1.5–2 h

places.name: Capuchos Convent
places.summary: Tiny 16th-century Franciscan friary built among boulders and lined with cork, a striking contrast to Sintra's palaces.
facts: Remote in the forest; car or taxi needed
Low doorways and tight cells
Allow about 1 h

places.name: Cabo da Roca
places.summary: Windswept cape with a lighthouse that is mainland Europe's westernmost point, with high cliffs over the Atlantic.
facts: Free; small paid car park
Very windy — bring a jacket
Sunset is popular; bus 403 from Sintra or Cascais
places.caution: Stay behind the barriers; the cliff edges are unstable and very high.

places.name: Praia da Ursa
places.summary: Wild, sea-stack-studded beach just north of Cabo da Roca, often called one of Portugal's most beautiful, reached only by a steep footpath.
facts: Park on the dirt area off the Cabo da Roca road
Steep, loose 20–30 min descent and harder climb back
No facilities or lifeguards
places.caution: Dangerous currents and a slippery trail; don't attempt in wet weather or wearing sandals.

places.name: Praia da Adraga
places.summary: Cove beach framed by cliffs and rock arches, with sea caves to explore at low tide and a beach restaurant.
facts: Car park at the end of the road from Almoçageme
Explore the arches and caves at low tide
Cold water year-round
places.caution: Strong waves and currents; check tide times before entering caves.

places.name: Azenhas do Mar
places.summary: Whitewashed cliffside village cascading down to a natural ocean pool — one of the most photographed spots on the Sintra coast.
facts: Best photo from the roadside viewpoint south of the village
Ocean pool fills at high tide in summer
Limited parking

places.name: Boca do Inferno
places.summary: Collapsed sea cave west of Cascais where Atlantic swells boom into the rocky chasm.
facts: Free; 20 min walk from Cascais centre
Most dramatic with big swell or stormy seas
Small craft market by the car park

places.name: Guincho Beach
places.summary: Big, wild Atlantic beach backed by dunes and the Sintra hills, a top kitesurf and windsurf spot.
facts: Free parking along the road
Very windy — great for kites, less so for sunbathing
Reachable by the Cascais coastal bike path (~9 km)
places.caution: Strong currents and rips; swim only near lifeguards in summer.

places.name: Setúbal
places.summary: Working port town on the Sado estuary with a lively fish market and a good old centre, gateway to Arrábida and the ferry to Tróia.
facts: Try choco frito (fried cuttlefish) and local seafood
Mercado do Livramento is best in the morning (closed Mondays)
Ferries to Tróia leave from the waterfront

places.name: Arrábida Natural Park
places.summary: Limestone range dropping steeply into turquoise sea, covered in Mediterranean scrub; the coastal and ridge roads (N379-1) offer spectacular viewpoints.
facts: Drive the scenic ridge road from Setúbal towards Portinho and Sesimbra
Several viewpoints with roadside pull-offs
Good hiking trails on the ridge
places.caution: Narrow, winding roads; in summer the coastal road is restricted and parking is limited.

places.name: Portinho da Arrábida
places.summary: Sheltered bay with calm, clear water and white sand beneath the green Arrábida cliffs, one of the region's best swimming spots.
facts: Calm, warmer water than the open Atlantic
Car access restricted on summer weekends — shuttle from Setúbal
Seafood restaurants by the bay
places.season: Sea pleasant June–September; quiet and lovely for a walk off-season.

places.name: Galapinhos Beach
places.summary: Small, unspoilt beach in Arrábida with clear turquoise water, reached by a steep path from the road.
facts: Park along the road and walk down 10–15 min
No facilities — bring water
Neighbouring Galápos beach has a café
places.caution: Steep path; parking is very limited and strictly controlled in summer.

places.name: Arrábida Convent
places.summary: 16th-century Franciscan convent clinging to the green slope of the Serra da Arrábida, with cells and chapels above the sea.
facts: Visits only by guided tour with prior booking (Fundação Oriente)
Great views of the coast

places.name: Sesimbra
places.summary: Fishing town in a sunny south-facing bay with a beach right in front of the old centre and excellent grilled fish restaurants.
facts: Town beach with calm water
Castle on the hill above town
Busy with Lisbon day-trippers on summer weekends

places.name: Sesimbra Castle
places.summary: Moorish-origin castle on a hill above Sesimbra with walls to walk and wide views over the bay and Arrábida.
facts: Free entry
Drive up or a steep walk from town
Allow 30–45 min

places.name: Cabo Espichel
places.summary: Remote, windswept cape with a lighthouse, a baroque pilgrimage sanctuary with pilgrim lodgings, and dinosaur footprints in the cliffs.
facts: Free; parking at the sanctuary
Beautiful at sunset
Dinosaur tracks are visible at Pedra da Mua cliff
places.caution: Sheer unfenced cliffs; keep well back, especially in wind.

places.name: Palmela Castle
places.summary: Hilltop castle above Palmela town with a pousada inside and panoramic views over Arrábida, the Sado and on clear days Lisbon.
facts: Free to walk the walls
Good stop on the way between Lisbon and Setúbal
Palmela is a wine region — try Moscatel

places.name: José Maria da Fonseca winery (Azeitão)
places.summary: Historic family winery in Vila Nogueira de Azeitão, famous for Moscatel de Setúbal and Periquita, with old cellars and a museum.
facts: Guided tours with tasting; book ahead
Buy Azeitão cheese and tortas nearby
Allow about 1–1.5 h

places.name: Sado dolphin-watching boat trip
places.summary: Boat trips from Setúbal into the Sado estuary to see its small resident population of bottlenose dolphins, with views of Arrábida and Tróia.
facts: Trips ~3 h from Setúbal harbour; book with licensed operators
Sightings likely but not guaranteed
Bring a windproof layer
places.season: Trips may be cancelled in rough weather.

places.name: Tróia Peninsula
places.summary: Long sandy peninsula across the Sado from Setúbal with calm estuary beaches, ocean beaches and the Roman fish-salting ruins of Cetóbriga.
facts: Ferry or catamaran from Setúbal (catamaran ~15 min; car ferry longer)
Resort area at the tip; wild beaches further south
Roman ruins have limited opening times
places.season: Ferry may be disrupted in rough seas.

places.name: Comporta
places.summary: Low-key village among rice fields and pine forests with vast, empty Atlantic beaches; a stylish but laid-back retreat.
facts: Combine with the stilt-pier fishing harbour of Carrasqueira
Storks nest in the rice fields
Beach restaurants are busy in summer — book
places.caution: Atlantic beaches here have strong currents; swim where lifeguards are present.

places.name: Costa da Caparica
places.summary: Near-continuous strip of sandy Atlantic beaches south of Lisbon across the Tagus, from busy town beaches to quieter dune stretches further south.
facts: ~25 min by car from Lisbon via the 25 de Abril Bridge (heavy summer weekend traffic)
Southern beaches (Fonte da Telha) are quieter
Good surf lessons
places.caution: Atlantic currents; swim only at lifeguarded beaches.
